title: Book Two · Chapter 99: Jun Wants His Own Part
story:
On Friday, Jun asks Ronan about the booklet for next term. They are putting their things away after the reading lesson. Miss Wu has not given them any materials to take home.

“Do you still want to do it?” Jun asks.

“Yes. With you.”

“I want my own part too.”

Ronan stops with a pencil in his hand. “You can draw.”

“I do not want only the pictures.”

Jun looks directly at him. Ronan remembers the shared bowl story and the card they repaired. He also remembers his words about the old practice. He told Jun he had no problems. He did have a wrong answer. His neck still feels hot at the memory.

“What part do you want?” he asks.

“We can decide with Miss Wu. I want to read and check things too.”

Ronan puts his pencil down. He wants the words. He wants the teacher to see his clear lines. He wants her to ask him about them. But Jun wants to do real work too. He does not just want to hold Ronan's things.

“All right,” Ronan says. “Both of us check. I can take care of the words too.”

“Check them against the real places?”

“Yes. And ask when we need to.”

Jun shuts his pencil case. He does not smile at once. Then he nods.

“Let us tell her on Monday.”

They leave the room together. In the yard, Leo asks what they are planning. Ronan tells him about next term. Leo is still unsure about a school task. His Saturday reading will continue, and he wants time for other things.

“You can read ours when it is ready,” Ronan says.

“If it is ready,” Jun adds.

Ronan looks at him. Jun grins, and Ronan laughs too. There is no book yet. They have no title or route yet. They have no page to show.

After school, Ronan takes the long way home with Jun as far as the corner. They talk about the summer. Then they pass a gate. A very large dog is behind it. They start to talk about the dog. The dog yawns through their whole conversation.

At home, Ronan puts his school things on the shelf. He opens his own birthday book to a clean page. For a moment, he imagines a booklet title there. Then he draws the yawning dog instead.

Mum asks what he and Jun will do. He says they want to help next term. Miss Wu has not chosen them yet. He does not say she has. On Monday, they still need to tell her together.
